page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.3xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at 3.2 GHz. It features 12 dedicated physical cores and 12 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. The system is equipped with 48.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data places the ecs.cm4.3xlarge in the average performance tier for most compute and memory operations. The stress-ng single-core score is 1575.58, and the multi-core score is 12474.34. Memory bandwidth tests show 698.22 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 55.6 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 46.36 GB/sec for large-block writes. The Passmark memory score is relatively weak at 1777.75, and the CPU physics test also scores in the lower tier at 741.78. However, database operations and Redis SET performance remain solid, with Redis achieving 11.64 million operations per second.

Given the 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated CPU allocation, this instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, web serving, and moderate database operations. It handles lightweight LLM inference well, achieving 144.53 tokens per second on a 135M model, though performance drops significantly to 6.99 tokens per second on a 7B model. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which should be factored into deployment designs.
